objective: Phase 2 of the data-collection audit: recompress and right-size storage for data that is already safely on disk (price_history.parquet, altdata panels, the 485 existing intraday partition files), and fix the one active I/O inefficiency (altdata _covered_dates full-panel read). No capture-path behavior changes -- this is storage/codec only, and depends on Phase 1 (docs/specs/intraday_capture_integrity_contract.json) for the intraday-corpus migration piece specifically.

prerequisites.independent_now: R1-R8 and scenarios 1-8 touch only io_utils.py, parquet_codec.py, backfill/price/runner.py, backfill/altdata/runner.py -- all exist today and have no dependency on Phase 1.
prerequisites.depends_on_phase1: R9 and scenarios 9-11 (intraday corpus migration) import normalize_bar_frame/normalize_tick_frame/assert_canonical_bars/assert_canonical_ticks from src/data/intraday_schema.py and the merge-safe writers from src/data/intraday_store.py as specified in docs/specs/intraday_capture_integrity_contract.json. Implement Phase 1 first; migrating the 485 legacy files into a schema Phase 1 hasn't landed yet would just recreate the KIS/LS unit collision this whole audit started from.

evidence.price_history_measured: data/history/price_history.parquet: 233.3MB, 5,046,547 rows, all-float64/object dtypes, snappy. Nullable-Int32 OHLC/prev_close + float32 levels + category symbol/market + zstd(level 6) + sort(symbol,date) measured 154.2MB (34% reduction). daily_change_pct kept float64 per quant.md; float32 roundtrip error on it measured max abs 1.46e-5 / mean 6.25e-9, and full-history compounding drift on a 50-symbol sample measured max relative 3.2e-5 -- small, but quant.md's 'retain float64 for compounding returns' is explicit and the column costs only ~30MB uncompressed, so the downcast is not taken.
evidence.altdata_measured: zstd(level 6) + category(symbol) + sort(symbol,date), values unchanged, int64 dtypes unchanged: program_trade_daily.parquet 117.5MB->84.6MB (28%), credit_balance.parquet 70.6MB->42.2MB (40%), shorting.parquet 45.1MB->30.7MB (32%). All measured against the live files in this repo.
evidence.value_range_check: volume column max = 2,498,359,659 > int32 max (2,147,483,647) -- MUST stay int64, downcasting it would silently overflow. prev_close has 66 NaN and at least one negative value (-92000.0, a pre-existing upstream data-quality artifact, out of scope to correct here) -- OHLC/prev_close must use a nullable integer dtype, not plain int32.
evidence.covered_dates_waste: src/backfill/altdata/runner.py::_covered_dates only needs the 'date' column but calls pd.read_parquet(panel_path) unconditionally, reading all 8 columns of a 113MB file (program_trade_daily) to extract one. columns=['date'] reads ~0.03MB per the per-column compressed-size breakdown already measured for this file -- roughly 3800x less I/O, invoked on every altdata backfill run for every one of the (currently 7) panels.
evidence.duplicate_writer: src/backfill/altdata/runner.py::_atomic_write_parquet (line 88) reimplements src/data/io_utils.py::atomic_write_parquet with no compression control and a slightly different tmp-file naming scheme -- a second, independently-maintained atomic-write path with no compression policy applied.
evidence.price_runner_writer: src/backfill/price/runner.py::_to_parquet already sorts by (symbol, date) before every write (line ~103), so the symbol,date sort order this contract adopts for price_history.parquet is already the production convention -- no downstream ordering assumption is broken by the migration. It calls df.to_parquet(parquet_path, index=False) with no compression argument (defaults to snappy, no dtype policy).

assumptions_and_invariants: This is a codec-and-dtype change only. No column is added, removed, or renamed on price_history.parquet or the altdata panels; no row is dropped; no numeric value's meaning changes. Every downcast must round-trip exactly for integer columns and within a stated tolerance for float32 columns.

Per quant.md 'Precision Validation', a float64->float32 downcast requires numerical-error validation before being applied. daily_change_pct, kospi_pct, and kosdaq_pct are return/percentage-change columns that may feed compounding calculations downstream (src/ml/exit_policy.py, src/ml/sector_features.py) and are kept float64 unconditionally -- they are NOT candidates for downcast in this contract, regardless of measured error.
market_cap_100m, trade_value_100m, foreign_netbuy, inst_netbuy, program_netbuy, v_kospi, v_kosdaq are level/amount columns (not compounded), and are the only float64->float32 downcasts in scope.

Altdata integer columns (volumes, KRW amounts) are NOT narrowed to int32 in this contract -- only their compression codec, symbol dtype (category), and sort order change. The measured 28-40% zstd win already captures most of the available gain without taking on unverified per-column range risk across 10 years of history.

All migration scripts are one-time, idempotent, dry-run-capable CLIs that write a .bak backup before replacing an existing file (or skip the file, never partially write it) and verify round-trip integrity before the replacement becomes permanent. A verification failure leaves the original file untouched and is reported, not silently swallowed.

atomic_write_parquet's compression default changes for ALL callers (intraday_store, altdata runner via the new shared writer, price_history writer). This is deliberate -- it is the single codec policy point for every parquet write in the project; a caller needing snappy for some external-compat reason must now pass compression='snappy' explicitly.
out_of_scope: Migrating data/parquet/trade_log.parquet or data/parquet/theme.parquet (small, <3MB combined -- not worth the churn).
Re-deriving or correcting the prev_close negative-value / NaN data-quality artifact found during evidence gathering -- flagged for a separate data-quality task, not silently fixed here.
Altdata integer column range auditing / int32 downcast (see assumptions) -- a candidate follow-up once full-history min/max is verified per column.
Any change to what is collected or how vendors are routed -- that is Phase 1's scope entirely.

requirements.rule: This module is the single codec/dtype policy point for all non-orderbook parquet writes in the project. It must not import from src/backfill or src/daily (avoid cycles) -- only pandas/pyarrow and src/data/io_utils.
requirements.detail: Consolidates what is currently three independent, drifted write paths (io_utils.atomic_write_parquet, altdata runner's local _atomic_write_parquet, and bare df.to_parquet in price/runner.py) into one.

requirements.rule: downcast_price_history_frame returns a COPY (never mutates the input) with: symbol/market -> category; open/high/low/close/prev_close -> pandas nullable 'Int32' (values rounded to nearest integer before cast, since KRW prices are integral); volume -> plain int64 (unchanged, never narrowed); market_cap_100m/trade_value_100m/foreign_netbuy/inst_netbuy/program_netbuy/v_kospi/v_kosdaq -> float32; daily_change_pct/kospi_pct/kosdaq_pct -> float64 unchanged; date -> unchanged; row order -> sorted by (symbol, date) ascending. Any column present in the input that is not named above passes through unchanged (fail-open on unknown columns, not fail-closed -- this must never silently drop data).
requirements.detail: Rounding before Int32 cast must use pandas .round() (banker's rounding is acceptable -- KRW prices have no meaningful sub-1-won precision in this dataset, confirmed 0 fractional values in open/high/low/close today).

requirements.rule: downcast_price_history_frame raises ValueError, refusing to downcast, if any open/high/low/close/prev_close value after rounding falls outside int32 range [-2147483648, 2147483647], or if the volume column's max exceeds int64 range. This is a fail-closed guard against a future data change silently corrupting the archive, not dead code -- volume's current max (2,498,359,659) already exceeds int32, which is exactly why it stays int64.
requirements.detail: Do not guard against the daily_change_pct/kospi_pct/kosdaq_pct columns the same way -- they are never touched, so there is nothing to overflow.

requirements.rule: downcast_altdata_panel_frame returns a copy with: symbol -> category, row order sorted by (symbol, date) ascending, date -> unchanged. Every other column (all currently int64 count/value/ratio columns across the 7 altdata panels) passes through with its dtype UNCHANGED -- no integer narrowing in this contract (see assumptions).
requirements.detail: This function must work unmodified across all 7 altdata files (program_trade_daily, credit_balance, shorting, disclosure, derivatives_basis, corp_code_map, and any future panel) -- it must not hardcode a panel-specific column list; only 'symbol' and 'date' are special-cased, by name, when present.

requirements.rule: write_price_history_parquet(df, target_path) = atomic_write_parquet(downcast_price_history_frame(df), target_path, compression=INTRADAY_COMPRESSION, compression_level=PARQUET_COMPRESSION_LEVEL). write_altdata_panel_parquet is the same shape using downcast_altdata_panel_frame. Neither function may read target_path or merge with existing content -- merge/incremental logic stays in the caller (price/runner.py, altdata/runner.py already do this); these two functions are pure downcast-then-write.
requirements.detail: Keeps the merge/business logic exactly where it already lives (Prefer Minimal Change) -- this contract only replaces the final .to_parquet call in each caller.

requirements.rule: atomic_write_parquet's compression default changes from 'snappy' to 'zstd', and it gains compression_level: int | None = 6. The compression_level kwarg is passed to df.to_parquet(...) ONLY when compression == 'zstd' and compression_level is not None -- snappy does not accept a level argument in pyarrow and must not receive one.
requirements.detail: Existing callers that never specified compression (intraday_store.write_intraday_partition, write_tick_partition) get zstd for free with zero call-site changes -- this is the intended forward-collection win, not just a migration-time one.

requirements.rule: _covered_dates must call pd.read_parquet(panel_path, columns=['date']) instead of a full read. If the file lacks a 'date' column, catch the resulting exception and return an empty set exactly as the current bare-except-Exception fallback does today -- behavior on malformed files must not regress.
requirements.detail: This is the single active runtime inefficiency in the codebase found by this audit (not a one-time migration item) -- it fires on every altdata backfill invocation, for every panel, forever, until fixed.

requirements.rule: Delete the local _atomic_write_parquet body and make it call src.data.parquet_codec.write_altdata_panel_parquet(df, path); keep the function name and signature for call-site compatibility (both call sites at lines ~231 and ~269 stay unchanged).
requirements.detail: Removes a second, independently-maintained atomic-write implementation (Prefer Existing Implementation directive) and gives every altdata write zstd + category(symbol) + sort(symbol,date) automatically, going forward, with no change to the values written.

requirements.rule: _to_parquet's two df.to_parquet(...) calls (the merged-with-existing branch and the fresh-file branch) are both replaced with src.data.parquet_codec.write_price_history_parquet(merged_or_df, parquet_path). The existing pd.concat / dropna / sort_values / drop_duplicates merge logic above the write is unchanged.
requirements.detail: This is what stops the codec/dtype regression from recurring -- without this wiring, the next backfill run would re-write price_history.parquet back to float64/object/snappy even after the one-time migration below.

requirements.rule: migrate_price_history_file(source_path, dry_run, backup) reads source_path, computes downcast_price_history_frame(df), and BEFORE writing anything verifies: (a) row count unchanged, (b) every Int32 column exactly equals round(original) after casting back to float64 (no value drift), (c) every float32 column's round-trip relative error is <= 1e-4, (d) daily_change_pct/kospi_pct/kosdaq_pct are byte-identical to the source (untouched). Any verification failure returns a dict with status='verification_failed' and writes NOTHING -- the source file is never touched on failure.
requirements.detail: On success and dry_run=False: copy source_path to source_path.with_suffix('.parquet.bak') when backup=True (skip if backup=False or a .bak already exists -- never overwrite a prior backup), then call write_price_history_parquet, then return a dict with status='migrated', original_size_bytes, new_size_bytes, rows. On dry_run=True: run verification and report the WOULD-BE new_size_bytes (by writing to a throwaway temp path and measuring, then discarding it) without touching source_path or writing any .bak.

requirements.rule: migrate_altdata_panel_file follows the identical contract shape as R10 (dry_run/backup/verification-before-write/status dict), using downcast_altdata_panel_frame and write_altdata_panel_parquet, applied per-file across the panel list in src/backfill/altdata/config.py's _ALTDATA_PANELS filenames (not hardcoded a second time in this script).
requirements.detail: Verification here only needs exact equality on every column except symbol (category vs original dtype, compared by value not dtype) and row order -- no float32 tolerance branch exists since no altdata column is downcast.

requirements.rule: detect_intraday_vendor(df) returns 'ls' when {'date','time','open','high','low','close','jdiff_vol','value'} subset is present natively, 'kis' when 'stck_cntg_hour' is present, and raises ValueError naming the actual column set otherwise -- never guesses. migrate_intraday_partition_file groups the file by its symbol column (종목코드), asserts every group has exactly one distinct snapshot-date value (raise ValueError on a file spanning multiple dates -- that violates the date-partition invariant this whole store is built on), calls normalize_bar_frame or normalize_tick_frame (per kind) per symbol group with vendor=detect_intraday_vendor(group), concatenates, and writes through intraday_store.write_intraday_partition / write_tick_partition (not a raw to_parquet) so the migrated file benefits from the same assert_canonical_* gate as forward collection.
requirements.detail: REQUIRES Phase 1 (src/data/intraday_schema.py, src/data/intraday_store.py's merge-safe writers) to be implemented first -- see prerequisites. For tick files specifically: truncated is set to False for every migrated row (this script has no way to know retroactively which pre-Phase-1 files were silently cut by the old max_pages=100 cap) -- it must NOT fabricate a per-row True/False guess. Instead it writes a companion `<file>.truncation_audit.json` recording, per symbol, the earliest captured ts_hms, so a human can cross-reference it against known-affected (date,symbol) pairs (e.g. the 2026-09-04 cases already identified: 032940, 108490, 336260, 030530, 014950) without the script inventing certainty it doesn't have.

requirements.rule: Every migration script is idempotent: running it twice on an already-migrated file must be a no-op on the second run (detected by checking the file's stored compression codec via pyarrow metadata -- if it already reads 'zstd', skip with status='already_migrated' and do not touch the file or create a new .bak). Each script exposes a CLI with --dry-run and --no-backup flags (argparse, matching the existing src/tools/migrate_sqlite_to_parquet.py convention) and, on completion, prints one summary line per file in the [DATA] tag format (logging.md): e.g. `[DATA] file=price_history.parquet status=migrated orig_mb=233.3 new_mb=154.2 rows=5046547`.
requirements.detail: Idempotency is what makes these safe to re-run after an interrupted first pass -- required, not optional, per the Retry Budget Boundary / fail-closed directives already governing this codebase.

requirements.rule: Every downcast/write function must be covered by a round-trip test that writes to a pytest tmp_path, reads it back, and asserts BOTH the dtype policy and the value preservation (not just 'it ran without raising') -- this mirrors testing.md's Contract Verification Over Empirical Validation and prevents a silent precision regression from passing CI.
requirements.detail: No test may assert only file size shrank; every scenario below asserts values first, size second (when size is asserted at all).

cli_entrypoints.self_wiring: main() calls migrate_price_history_file(settings.PRICE_HISTORY_PARQUET_PATH, dry_run=args.dry_run, backup=not args.no_backup) and prints the [DATA] summary line; this is the ONLY caller, run once manually.
cli_entrypoints.note: target_file for this script is created by this contract; it is a new file and therefore intentionally excluded from the `wiring` array (lean_check's pre-impl wiring check requires the caller_file to already exist -- see docs/specs/intraday_capture_integrity_contract.json's identical pattern for collect_auction.py).

cli_entrypoints.self_wiring: main() iterates _ALTDATA_PANELS filenames under settings.ALTDATA_DIR and calls migrate_altdata_panel_file per existing file.

main() globs data/history/intraday/{1m,ticks}/**/*.parquet and calls migrate_intraday_partition_file per file, writing data/history/intraday/_migration_manifest.json on completion. Depends on Phase 1 -- see prerequisites.

def test_downcast_price_history_frame_preserves_values_across_dtype_change() -> None:
    import pandas as pd

    from src.data.parquet_codec import downcast_price_history_frame

    df = pd.DataFrame(
        {
            "date": pd.to_datetime(["2026-01-02", "2026-01-02", "2026-01-01"]),
            "symbol": ["005930", "000660", "005930"],
            "open": [70000.0, 130000.0, 69000.0],
            "high": [70500.0, 131000.0, 69500.0],
            "low": [69800.0, 129500.0, 68900.0],
            "close": [70200.0, 130500.0, 69200.0],
            "prev_close": [69200.0, float("nan"), 68000.0],
            "market_cap_100m": [4190000.5, 950000.25, 4180000.0],
            "trade_value_100m": [12345.678, 5432.1, 11000.0],
            "daily_change_pct": [0.01445086705202312, float("nan"), 0.0176],
            "market": ["KOSPI", "KOSPI", "KOSPI"],
            "volume": [15000000, 8000000, 14000000],
            "foreign_netbuy": [1000.0, -500.0, 900.0],
            "inst_netbuy": [200.0, 100.0, 150.0],
            "program_netbuy": [50000000.0, -20000000.0, 40000000.0],
            "kospi_pct": [0.005, 0.005, 0.004],
            "kosdaq_pct": [0.003, 0.003, 0.002],
            "v_kospi": [18.5, 18.5, 19.0],
            "v_kosdaq": [float("nan"), float("nan"), float("nan")],
        }
    )

    out = downcast_price_history_frame(df)

    assert str(out["open"].dtype) == "Int32"
    assert str(out["prev_close"].dtype) == "Int32"
    assert pd.isna(out.loc[out["symbol"] == "000660", "prev_close"].iloc[0])
    assert out["open"].dropna().astype("int64").tolist() == [69000, 70000, 130000] or set(out["open"].dropna().tolist()) == {69000, 70000, 130000}
    assert str(out["symbol"].dtype) == "category"
    assert str(out["volume"].dtype) in ("int64", "Int64")
    assert str(out["market_cap_100m"].dtype) == "float32"
    for orig, new in zip(df["market_cap_100m"].sort_values(), out["market_cap_100m"].astype("float64").sort_values()):
        assert abs(orig - new) / max(abs(orig), 1e-9) < 1e-4
    assert out["date"].is_monotonic_increasing or list(out["date"]) == sorted(out["date"])

def test_downcast_price_history_frame_rejects_int32_overflow() -> None:
    import pandas as pd
    import pytest

    from src.data.parquet_codec import downcast_price_history_frame

    base = {
        "date": pd.to_datetime(["2026-01-02"]), "symbol": ["005930"],
        "open": [70000.0], "high": [70500.0], "low": [69800.0], "close": [70200.0], "prev_close": [69200.0],
        "market_cap_100m": [1.0], "trade_value_100m": [1.0], "daily_change_pct": [0.01],
        "market": ["KOSPI"], "volume": [2_498_359_659],
        "foreign_netbuy": [1.0], "inst_netbuy": [1.0], "program_netbuy": [1.0],
        "kospi_pct": [0.01], "kosdaq_pct": [0.01], "v_kospi": [18.5], "v_kosdaq": [18.5],
    }

    ok = downcast_price_history_frame(pd.DataFrame(base))
    assert str(ok["volume"].dtype) in ("int64", "Int64")
    assert int(ok["volume"].iloc[0]) == 2_498_359_659

    bad = dict(base)
    bad["close"] = [3_000_000_000.0]
    with pytest.raises(ValueError):
        downcast_price_history_frame(pd.DataFrame(bad))

def test_atomic_write_parquet_defaults_to_zstd_compression(tmp_path) -> None:
    import pandas as pd
    import pyarrow.parquet as pq

    from src.data.io_utils import atomic_write_parquet

    target = tmp_path / "out.parquet"
    atomic_write_parquet(pd.DataFrame({"a": [1, 2, 3]}), target)

    meta = pq.ParquetFile(target).metadata
    codec = meta.row_group(0).column(0).compression
    assert codec.upper() == "ZSTD"


def test_atomic_write_parquet_snappy_override_still_works(tmp_path) -> None:
    import pandas as pd
    import pyarrow.parquet as pq

    from src.data.io_utils import atomic_write_parquet

    target = tmp_path / "out.parquet"
    atomic_write_parquet(pd.DataFrame({"a": [1, 2, 3]}), target, compression="snappy")

    meta = pq.ParquetFile(target).metadata
    assert meta.row_group(0).column(0).compression.upper() == "SNAPPY"

def test_altdata_covered_dates_reads_only_date_column(tmp_path, monkeypatch) -> None:
    import pandas as pd

    from src.backfill.altdata import runner

    path = tmp_path / "panel.parquet"
    pd.DataFrame({"date": pd.to_datetime(["2026-01-02"]), "symbol": ["005930"], "value": [1]}).to_parquet(path, index=False)

    seen_kwargs = {}
    real_read_parquet = pd.read_parquet

    def spy_read_parquet(p, *args, **kwargs):
        seen_kwargs.update(kwargs)
        return real_read_parquet(p, *args, **kwargs)

    monkeypatch.setattr(runner.pd, "read_parquet", spy_read_parquet)

    result = runner._covered_dates(path)

    assert seen_kwargs.get("columns") == ["date"]
    assert len(result) == 1

def test_altdata_atomic_write_parquet_delegates_to_shared_codec(tmp_path) -> None:
    import pandas as pd
    import pyarrow.parquet as pq

    from src.backfill.altdata import runner

    path = tmp_path / "panel.parquet"
    df = pd.DataFrame({"date": pd.to_datetime(["2026-01-02", "2026-01-01"]), "symbol": ["000660", "005930"], "value": [1, 2]})

    runner._atomic_write_parquet(df, path)

    meta = pq.ParquetFile(path).metadata

    import pandas as pd

    import src.tools.migrate_price_history_storage as mod

    path = tmp_path / "price_history.parquet"
    cols = {
        "date": pd.to_datetime(["2026-01-02"]), "symbol": ["005930"],
        "open": [70000.0], "high": [70500.0], "low": [69800.0], "close": [70200.0], "prev_close": [69200.0],
        "market_cap_100m": [1.0], "trade_value_100m": [1.0], "daily_change_pct": [0.01],

        "kospi_pct": [0.01], "kosdaq_pct": [0.01], "v_kospi": [18.5], "v_kosdaq": [18.5],
    }
    pd.DataFrame(cols).to_parquet(path, index=False)
    original_bytes = path.read_bytes()

    def corrupt_downcast(df):
        out = df.copy()
        out["daily_change_pct"] = 999.0  # 검증 실패를 강제로 유발
        return out

    monkeypatch.setattr(mod, "downcast_price_history_frame", corrupt_downcast)

    result = mod.migrate_price_history_file(path, dry_run=False)

    assert result["status"] == "verification_failed"
    assert path.read_bytes() == original_bytes
    assert not path.with_suffix(".parquet.bak").exists()

2. Run `uv run python -m src.tools.migrate_price_history_storage --dry-run` and `... migrate_altdata_storage --dry-run`, inspect the printed size deltas, then re-run without --dry-run.

3. Only after Phase 1 (intraday_capture_integrity_contract.json) is merged, run `uv run python -m src.tools.migrate_intraday_corpus --dry-run`, review the resulting truncation_audit.json files against the known-affected 2026-09-04 symbols, then re-run without --dry-run.
4. Delete the .bak files only after spot-checking a handful of migrated files against their originals -- this is a manual, human-gated step, not automated by any script in this contract.
